verses.text: 142. By his Revelation, “the invisible God, from the fullness of his love, addresses men as his friends, and moves among them, in order to invite and receive them into his own company.” (DV 2; cf. Col 1:15; 1 Tim 1:17; Ex 33:11; Jn 15:14–15; Bar 3:38 (Vulg.).) The adequate response to this invitation is faith.

210. After Israel’s sin, when the people had turned away from God to worship the golden calf, God hears Moses’ prayer of intercession and agrees to walk in the midst of an unfaithful people, thus demonstrating his love. (Cf. Ex 32; 33:12–17.) When Moses asks to see his glory, God responds “I will make all my goodness pass before you, and will proclaim before you my name ‘the Lord’ [YHWH].” (Ex 33:18–19.) Then the Lord passes before Moses and proclaims, “YHWH, YHWH, a God merciful and gracious, slow to anger, and abounding in steadfast love and faithfulness”; Moses then confesses that the Lord is a forgiving God. (Ex 34:5–6; cf. 34:9.)
